summary: Foundations for child chats, behind the staged flag hub_children (HUB_CHILDREN_ENABLED in src/shared/hub.ts, false; SB_HUB_CHILDREN=1 or the backend setting labs.hub_children turns it on). Any chat can become a parent; there is no chat type and no column on conversations. This change adds the tables hub_parents, hub_batches, hub_children and hub_wakes (a wake holds a summary and a pointer into the child's transcript, never a report body), their CRUD with every conversation id resolved to its root, the hub.* settings with defaults and ranges (no UI yet), and the pure rules childState, parentState, grantedMode, hubNeedsCard (a card only in plan and supervised modes), runSlotFree, wakeBatchDecision, the pointer parser and the brief and update wrappers, with shared fixtures. Nothing reads the flag outside tests, so no behaviour changes. The migration time is logged through the db.migrate perf span. Starting children (PR 5): with the flag on, every chat that is not an open child gets the MCP tools start_children and list_children and a short hub paragraph in its MCP instructions. start_children (1 to 8 tasks) opens one approval card in plan and supervised modes (plan mode itself is refused) and starts at once in auto-accept edits and above, with a stored row that lists the children. The same plan twice returns the open card. A child gets min(requested, parent) as its mode, its own worktree (purpose hub-child, branch namespace hub) or the project folder, and every node_modules folder of the project cloned before its first turn, which is the brief wrapped in <switchboard-hub-brief>. The batch is refused when free disk after it would fall under hub.minFreeGiB (5 GiB). At most hub.runningPerInstance (3) children per account and hub.runningPerParent (6) per parent run a turn at once; the others wait for a slot. One failed child becomes failed_start with a failed wake, and the batch goes on; a child cut off by a quit gets the same at the next start. The backend refuses a user turn to an open child (code child_read_only, on SUBMIT_USER_TURN and SEND_TURN, so every client and transport), and a peer message to it from anyone but its parent. A child gets no parent tools. Measured: perf spans hub.batch, hub.start-child (worktree, clone and launch times, disk use), hub.child-turn (tokens, cost, duration per child turn) and hub.resources (every 30 s while children are open: RSS, CPU % and process count of each child's and parent's agent process tree, the app's main heap, renderer CPU and total RSS). Linked dependencies (PR 6): each child's dependency folders (every node_modules next to a package.json up to 3 levels down, plus worktree.link paths from the launch config) are linked to the main checkout by default (setting hub.childDependencies: link, clone, install or none). Rules L1 to L5 move a folder down the chain link, clone, install, none: an install script (preinstall, install, postinstall) or workspaces clone; a base commit whose package.json or lockfile differs from the main checkout installs (frozen: npm ci, pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, yarn install --immutable); an installed tree that differs from the lockfile clones; links on macOS, Linux and Windows (a directory junction there, which needs no admin rights), clones only on macOS and Linux, so Windows installs where it would clone. The write guard compares paths case-insensitively on Windows. A link is listed in the repository's info/exclude (no trailing slash), so git status stays clean, and in switchboard-dep-links.json in the worktree's git folder, which removeWorktree reads to unlink before git removes the worktree. The brief says which folders are linked. After each child turn the links, the child's lockfile and the install record in each linked folder are compared with link time; a change stops the child with a blocked wake. An open child gets the MCP tool own_dependencies, which swaps each link for its own clone (or a frozen install). The file write and delete IPC refuses a path inside a child's linked folder. The batch card's disk need counts a link as nothing, a clone as 5% of the folder and an install as the whole folder. Measured: hub.start-child reports linked, cloned, installed and none counts and the dependency time; hub.deps-check times each post-turn check and its outcome; hub.own-deps each own_dependencies call. Desktop UI (PR 7): with the flag on, session list rows carry an optional hub field ({ parentId } on an open child, { openChildren } on its parent), and the sidebar nests open children under their parent with a fold caret, and Recent leaves children out. The channel provider:hub-list-children returns a chat's hub view: the chat itself, its parent while it is an open child, and its unsettled children with childState, account, branch, last turn tokens and known cost, and last update, plus parentState. The event hub.children-changed (the parent's root id) fires when a child is added, opens, fails or gets a wake, and on a child's status change (not a repeated status), turn end, card or limit change, and the desktop re-reads at most once per 250 ms; the desktop hub-store re-reads only the chats on screen. A parent shows a Hub chip in its header and the children strip above its composer (Open, Nudge, Stop while Working). An open child shows a banner in place of its chat input (Stop while it runs, Message the hub); its activity row stays and its approval and question cards still answer. Nudge and Message the hub open the parent with a "To: <child>" chip that asks the parent agent to pass the words on with send_agent_message. Measured: the perf span hub.view times each view read with its child count (info above 100 ms, debug below). Lineage messages (PR 8): with the flag on, each open child and its parent share a lineage edge, rebuilt from hub_children at startup and when a child row changes. Along it send_agent_message needs no approval card in any mode but plan (plan denies it), and the two may send 60 messages, renewed when the user writes in either chat; the edge has no time window and outlives /unlink, a stop and an archive. An open child's agent may message only its parent, and /link with an open child on either side is refused (child_read_only text). list_agent_sessions marks the parent and the children (hub: parent or child). send_agent_message takes delivery: queue (default) or steer, also kept on its card: an idle chat gets an ordinary turn; a busy one gets a steer only when asked, where the agent can steer (Claude, Codex), and not while its turn is compacting or being stopped; every other case queues behind the running turn, so a busy ACP child (OpenCode, Gemini) gets the message after its turn instead of a refusal. A peer message is still an ordinary turn and cannot answer an approval. A spent lineage budget refuses the send without a Not delivered row (its Send would be a user message to the child), and the agent is told to report it. The /send-to channel ignores a delivery a client sends. Without the flag nothing changes: no lineage edge, no delivery argument, and a busy ACP target still refuses. Measured: each delivered message logs lineage, the requested delivery and the delivery used on its peer message delivered line, which counts lineage traffic and steer fallbacks; lineage links synced logs each resync. Screenshot tests and routing (hub PR 7 follow-up): Stop in the children strip goes to the backend of the parent (preload provider.interruptHubChild, RoutingTable.resolveThread over the parent's thread ids), and Open, the banner's parent link and Message the hub open a chat that is not open here on the machine of the hub chat that is, because a parent starts its children on its own backend; before, both went to the local backend for a child on a remote machine that the user never opened. The strip's rows truncate, so a narrow chat column does not scroll sideways. The desktop hub UI uses the app's own row and chip styles: sidebar child rows sit a 22px step under the parent on a tree line with a CSS fold caret, a state dot and a state word read from the parent's hub view (the parent shows its open count); the Hub chip is a toolbar chip beside the chat identity (an open child shows a Child chip and its parent as a breadcrumb); the children strip has one line per child with Open, Nudge and Stop as text actions and the counts, parent state and tokens in its header; the child banner states read-only, links the parent title and offers Message the hub. Reports and wakes (PR 9): with the flag on, an open child gets the MCP tool report_to_hub { status: done, question or blocked, summary, report? }. Each call stores one hub_wakes row with the child's summary and a pointer (the provider's id of that tool call when the registry saw it start, the time, and the Claude JSONL or Codex rollout path); the report itself stays in the child's transcript and never reaches the parent's database. Every brief ends with a line that tells the child to report this way. Wakes, including the failed and blocked ones, go to the parent as one turn wrapped in <switchboard-hub-update> (a line per wake: title, state, summary, and a read_child line with the child id and the pointer), sent through the approval result path (no turnDepth, no link renewal) only while the parent's session is idle, 15 s after the newest wake. A wake counts as delivered once the agent shows output on that turn (text or a tool call); a refused send, a turn that ends without output, or one with none for 2 minutes (which is then ended), leaves its wakes pending for one more try, and a second failure holds them. Past 30 wake turns per parent in an hour the wakes are held too. A held parent shows Updates ready; the strip shows the number of held updates with Deliver, also after every child settled (channel provider:hub-deliver-held-wakes), and the user's next message to the parent carries every pending wake along in its own commit and lifts the hold. Each delivery stores a [[sb:hub-update]] row in the parent's chat (per child: title, what happened, summary, Open in child); the agent's update turn is dropped from the chat on desktop, Expo and Android (synthetic split, fixture cases). The parent gets read_child { childId, at?, offset?, limit?, query? }: one of its own children's history through the chat view's loader, starting at a pointer or an offset, else the newest 20 (at most 200), with a query searching the whole history, a report_to_hub call whole (a Codex or ACP child keeps at most 32 KiB of it in Switchboard's copy) and other tool input and output shortened, and the child's own subagent rows; when the transcript file a pointer names is gone it says so and gives the summary. list_children now shows each child's newest update, delivered or not. Measured: hub.wake perf line per wake turn (wakes, children, bytes, attempt, outcome, ms to the first activity, threshold 0), hub.read-child per call (messages, total, bytes, outcome), a child reported info line per report (status, summary bytes, pointer kind), wakes held and wakes carried on a user turn info lines. Stop, subagents and the idle reaper (PR 10): with the flag on, Stop on a chat with open children (the Stop button, or Stop all in the strip through provider:hub-stop-children) stops every open child in parallel, holds the parent's updates (hub_parents.held, reason stop) until the user's next message or Deliver, and disarms the auto-resume rows of the parent and its children. Stop on one child (strip, child view, phone) and the new parent tool interrupt_child { childId } (own open children only, denied in plan mode) stop its turn, disarm its auto-resume, close its open cards, expire its provider requests, cancel its queued messages and count its running subagents as failed; stopping a child with no running turn succeeds and changes nothing more. A running child that the user or its parent's Stop stopped gets one stopped wake; interrupt_child gets none, since the parent did it. Switchboard writes its own wakes, at most one per task (the brief or a message from the parent) and none after the child's own report: decided where the turn ends: a full context window is blocked, a usage limit writes none, a turn that ends on an error or an agent process that ends with an error is failed, and a turn that ends with no report and no subagent running, or a session that exits, is stopped. A session that Switchboard itself stops writes none. A child stopped while it is still starting gets no first turn and a stopped wake. A child's Agent and Task calls count as running until their result, a background agent until its completion notice: the child shows Working (Reported, subagents still running after a report) and list_children reports nativeSubagents { running, done, failed }. The idle reaper checks every 60 s: an open child whose last update is a report, with no subagent running and no turn, card or question, idle for hub.idleReapMinutes (20 by default) since its last turn end, has its session stopped and then every process of its agent's process tree that is still alive killed (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 2 s). Its parent's next message starts it again from its session. A parent is never reaped. Measured: hub.stop per parent Stop (children, stopped, failed, duration), hub.reap per reap (idle minutes, processes in the tree, killed, outcome), hub.resume-reaped per restart, and the info lines child stopped (by, running), child wake (kind) and idle child reaped.

desktop.followUpRelease: The release that turns hub_children on by default (HUB_CHILDREN_ENABLED true), after children ship on desktop, Expo and Android and one hub runs end to end on the beta channel.

reactNativeIos.followUpRelease: The release that turns hub_children on by default (HUB_CHILDREN_ENABLED true), after children ship on desktop, Expo and Android and one hub runs end to end on the beta channel. Until then a phone shows the batch card as an ordinary approval with its plain-text detail, and the backend refuses typing into a child. Phones ignore the session rows' hub field and the hub.children-changed event, and list children as top-level chats until the phone PRs. Child updates (PR 9): both phones drop the parent's <switchboard-hub-update> turn from the chat (shared synthetic split cases; Android SyntheticUserMessage.kt), and show the stored [[sb:hub-update]] row as a Switchboard notice until the phone contract PR gives it its own row. Stop (PR 10): a phone's Stop on a child, and on its parent, already reaches the backend's INTERRUPT, so the cascade, the hold and the stopped wakes apply to it; the phones get Stop all (provider:hub-stop-children) and the Working state of a child with running subagents in the phone PRs.

The labs switch reaches beta users first. This change touches no package identity, signing, deep link or native module, and its migration is additive, so an older build opens a migrated database.

automated: npx vitest run tests/unit/hub-rules.test.ts tests/unit/hub-db.test.ts --maxWorkers=2: childState, parentState, grantedMode, hubNeedsCard, runSlotFree and wakeBatchDecision pass every case in tests/fixtures/hub-cases.json; the flag helper is off by default and on with SB_HUB_CHILDREN=1 or labs.hub_children; readHubSettings keeps in-range values and falls back to defaults; hub_parents, hub_batches, hub_children and hub_wakes CRUD, the open-child lookup by child_id, wake delivery once per wake, and a rotated Claude id resolving to its root conversation.
A copy of a real 1.1 GB desktop database migrated with this build (five new tables, no other change), and the migrate code of origin/main then opened the migrated file.

notExercised: No live run with real agents: the batch card, worktree creation, the clone and the brief turn were not run in the app. The nested sidebar, the Hub chip, the children strip and the child banner now have screenshot tests with the demo adapter; Nudge was not run in the app.

Kill-the-app recovery of worktrees relies on the existing worktree creation recovery and was not run by hand. No child ran npm test through a real link in the app; the unit test reads a package through the link only.
The Android port of hub-cases.json is not written yet.

Agents' own file tools (Claude Write and Edit, Codex apply_patch, ACP writes) and the embedded IDE are not refused under a linked folder; only Switchboard's file write and delete IPC is. The post-turn check catches an install, a removal and a lockfile change, not an edit of one package file.
The frozen install fallback was not run (it needs the network); worktree.setup is not used as the install command.

Lineage messages against real Claude, Codex, OpenCode and Gemini sessions (a steer into a running Claude turn, a queued message to a running Gemini child) were not run; the registry tests use fake adapters.
Stop and Open from the strip for a child on a real remote machine were not run; only the routing table and the opener's machine choice have unit tests.

Stop, interrupt_child and the idle reaper were not run against real agents: the registry tests use a fake adapter, and the reaper's process kill was tested with a fake process table. The reaper keeps a reaped child's start options in memory: after an app restart that child starts the way any closed chat does. The open native subagent rows of a stopped child are not closed in the renderer; the backend counts them as failed. The legacy SEND_TURN channel does not lift a hold, as it carries no wakes.
